newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says EU Finance Ministers likely to meet.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says EU Finance Ministers likely to meet.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi said a meeting of European Union Finance Ministers was likely to be called for Sunday to settle problems over the lira's re-entry into the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), the Italian news agency ANSA reported.

The EU's monetary committee was meeting on Saturday to discuss the lira's ERM re-entry but a monetary official said talks had run into trouble and a meeting of EU finance ministers could be needed to iron out differences.

"Either it (the monetary committee meeting) finishes this evening or much more probably there will be a supplement to the talks involving Finance Ministers," Prodi told reporters outside his home in Bologna, ANSA reported.
Asked if he was optimistic that an agreement could be reached, Prodi replied: "How can you expect me not to be? We have prepared things seriously."
He added: "There is always the problem of what exchange rate to enter at. Evidently there are conflicting interests. These negotiations require time and discussion."
Rome hopes that by returning to the EU's currency grid it will enhance its chances of qualifying for the single European currency in 1999.
